# GitHub Actions - Automated Testing Workflows

This directory contains GitHub Actions workflows for automated testing of the 7monthIndicator Trading Bot.

## 📋 Available Workflows

### 1. Quick Tests (`quick-tests.yml`) ⚡

**Purpose:** Fast validation on every push and pull request

**Triggers:**
- Push to `main`, `develop`, or `binance` branches
- Pull requests to `main` or `develop`
- Manual dispatch
- When Python files or tests change

**What it does:**
- ✅ Runs unit tests in ~5 seconds
- ✅ Generates test results (JUnit XML)
- ✅ Creates coverage report
- ✅ Uploads results as artifacts (30 days retention)
- ✅ Comments on PRs with test results
- ✅ Uploads to Codecov (optional)

**Artifacts:**
- `test-results-{run_number}/` - Test results, coverage, logs

---

### 2. Full Test Suite (`full-tests.yml`) 🔍

**Purpose:** Comprehensive testing for releases and scheduled runs

**Triggers:**
- Push to `main` branch
- Pull requests to `main`
- Daily at 2 AM UTC (scheduled)
- Manual dispatch with options

**What it does:**
- ✅ Runs complete test suite (unit + integration)
- ✅ Generates comprehensive coverage reports
- ✅ Creates detailed test reports
- ✅ Uploads results as artifacts (90 days retention)
- ✅ Uploads to Codecov
- ✅ Publishes summary to GitHub

**Artifacts:**
- `full-test-results-{run_number}/` - Complete test results, coverage HTML, logs

---

### 3. Test Status Badge (`test-status-badge.yml`) 🎯

**Purpose:** Update test status badge

**Triggers:**
- After Quick Tests complete
- After Full Test Suite completes

**What it does:**
- ✅ Generates test status badge JSON
- ✅ Updates badge based on test results
- ✅ Shows passing/failing status

---

## 🚀 How to Use

### View Test Results

#### After Push/PR:

1. Go to **Actions** tab in GitHub
2. Select the workflow run
3. View the **Summary** page for test results
4. Download **Artifacts** for detailed reports

#### In Pull Requests:

- Test results are automatically commented on the PR
- Summary shows in the PR checks
- Coverage changes are highlighted

### Manual Workflow Dispatch

#### Quick Tests:

```
GitHub → Actions → Quick Tests → Run workflow
```

#### Full Test Suite:

```
GitHub → Actions → Full Test Suite → Run workflow
Options:
  - Enable/disable coverage report
```

---

## 📊 Test Results & Artifacts

### What Gets Uploaded

#### Quick Tests Artifacts:

```
test-results-{run_number}/
├── junit.xml              # JUnit test results
├── coverage.xml           # Coverage XML report
├── htmlcov/              # HTML coverage report
│   └── index.html
├── summary.md            # Test summary
└── test-output.log       # Complete test output
```

**Retention:** 30 days

#### Full Test Suite Artifacts:

```
full-test-results-{run_number}/
├── unit-tests.xml         # Unit test results
├── integration-tests.xml  # Integration test results
├── coverage.xml           # Coverage XML
├── htmlcov/              # HTML coverage
│   └── index.html
├── reports/
│   └── full-report.md    # Comprehensive report
└── test-output.log       # Complete output
```

**Retention:** 90 days

### Downloading Artifacts

1. Go to **Actions** tab
2. Click on a workflow run
3. Scroll to **Artifacts** section
4. Click to download ZIP file
5. Extract and view reports

## 🔧 Configuration

### Environment Variables

No secrets required for basic testing. Optional:

- `CODECOV_TOKEN` - For Codecov uploads (optional)

### Customize Triggers

Edit workflow files to change when tests run:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, develop, your-branch ]  # Add branches
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]
```

### Customize Retention

Change artifact retention period:

```yaml
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    retention-days: 30  # Change to 7, 30, 90, etc.
```

---

## 📈 Coverage Tracking

### Codecov Integration

If you have Codecov set up:

1. Add `CODECOV_TOKEN` to repository secrets
2. Workflows automatically upload coverage
3. View coverage at: `https://codecov.io/gh/{owner}/{repo}`

### Coverage Reports

HTML coverage reports show:
- Line-by-line coverage
- Branch coverage
- Function coverage
- Missing lines highlighted

Access via:
- Download artifact → Extract → Open `htmlcov/index.html`

---

## 🎯 Workflow Status

### View Status

- **Actions tab** - All workflow runs
- **README badges** - Add status badges (see below)
- **PR checks** - Shows in PR checks section

### Status Badges

Add to your README.md:

```markdown
![Quick Tests](https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/quick-tests.yml/badge.svg)
![Full Tests](https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/full-tests.yml/badge.svg)
```

Replace `{owner}` and `{repo}` with your GitHub username and repository name.

## 🐛 Troubleshooting

### Tests Fail in CI but Pass Locally

**Common causes:**
- Missing dependencies in `requirements.txt`
- Environment differences
- Timezone issues

**Solution:**
```bash
# Test locally with same Python version
python3.10 -m venv test-venv
source test-venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
./quick_test.sh
```

### Artifacts Not Uploading

**Check:**
- File paths in workflow exist
- Permissions are correct
- Artifact size < 10GB

### Workflow Taking Too Long

**Quick fixes:**
- Reduce test scope
- Use caching for dependencies
- Split into parallel jobs

---

## 🚀 Best Practices

### 1. Run Quick Tests Often

- Every commit
- Every PR
- Before merging

### 2. Run Full Suite Strategically

- Before releases
- On main branch
- Daily scheduled runs

### 3. Monitor Coverage

- Set coverage thresholds
- Track trends over time
- Aim for 80%+ coverage

### 4. Fix Failing Tests ASAP

- Don't ignore failing tests
- CI failures block merges
- Keep tests green

---

## 📝 Example Usage Scenarios

### Scenario 1: Feature Development

```
1. Create feature branch
2. Make changes
3. Push → Quick Tests run automatically
4. Review test results in Actions
5. Fix failures if any
6. Create PR → Tests run again
7. Review PR comment with results
8. Merge when tests pass
```

### Scenario 2: Release Preparation

```
1. Push to main branch
2. Both Quick and Full Tests run
3. Review comprehensive results
4. Download artifacts for records
5. Check coverage reports
6. Verify all tests pass
7. Deploy with confidence
```

### Scenario 3: Daily Monitoring

```
1. Scheduled run at 2 AM UTC
2. Full Test Suite executes
3. Results emailed (if configured)
4. Review any failures
5. Fix issues proactively
```
